faq.q: Is May a good month for a boat rental in Marbella?
faq.a: Yes, May is one of the best months. You get warm, settled weather with sea temperatures rising from 17°C to 20°C, plenty of sunshine (9–10 hours), and fewer crowds than June or July. Wind is usually light to moderate, so most days are comfortable for cruising, swimming, or just relaxing on deck.

faq.q: What is the sea temperature in Marbella in May?
faq.a: In early May, the sea is around 17–18°C. By the end of the month, it reaches 19–20°C. It's still a bit fresh for long swims, but many people do go in – especially if you're used to cooler water. A wetsuit or a quick dip is fine. The air is warmer, so you'll dry off quickly.

faq.q: How windy is it in Marbella in May?
faq.a: May typically has light to moderate winds, averaging 10–15 knots. The famous Poniente (west) wind can pick up in the afternoon, but it's usually not strong enough to cancel trips. Our skippers monitor conditions daily and will advise if any route needs adjusting – safety first.

faq.q: Can you swim in the sea in Marbella in May?
faq.a: You can, but it's brisk. Sea temperatures hover around 18–20°C, which is refreshing rather than warm. If you're planning a swim stop, consider a boat with a swim platform, like the Azimut 39 or the Astondoa 40. Most guests do take a dip, especially after a bit of sun.

faq.q: What is the best boat for May conditions in Marbella?
faq.a: For a group of up to 9–11, the Astondoa 40 (12.5m) or Azimut 39 (12.5m) are ideal – both are stable and fast, with plenty of shade. For a larger group (up to 12), the Azimut 58 Flybridge offers a spacious flybridge perfect for soaking up spring sun. All depart from Puerto Banús.

faq.q: How much does a boat rental in Marbella cost in May?
faq.a: Our Tier A boats – Astondoa 40 and Azimut 39 – cost €749 for 2 hours or €2,299 for a full day (8 hours). This includes skipper, fuel, drinks, snacks, and VAT. For the Mangusta 80, the minimum charter is 4 hours at €4,719, which includes a free jet ski. Other boats are priced on request via WhatsApp.

faq.q: Is it safe to rent a boat in May if the weather changes?
faq.a: Absolutely. All our skippers are licensed and experienced, and they have real-time weather updates. If a front moves in (rare in May), they'll adjust the route or suggest a shorter trip. Your safety is always the priority, and we'll reschedule or refund if conditions are unsafe.

faq.q: Do I need to book a boat in May in advance?
faq.a: Yes, especially for weekends and the last two weeks of May. May is popular for birthdays, stag/hen parties, and early summer holidays. We recommend booking at least 1–2 weeks ahead. You can check availability via WhatsApp – we usually reply within the hour.

data.body_html:
Thinking about a Marbella boat rental in May 2025? You're in for a treat. May is that sweet spot on the Costa del Sol: warm air, settled seas, and the crowds of July are still weeks away. Sea temperatures climb from 17°C to 20°C, and you'll get 9–10 hours of sunshine a day. In this guide, we break down the spring sea conditions – wind, waves, rain, and water temperature – so you know exactly what to expect when you step aboard in Puerto Banús.

May Sea Temperature in Marbella: What to Expect

In early May, the Mediterranean off Marbella sits at around 17–18°C. By the end of the month, it warms to 19–20°C. That's still a little fresh for a long swim, but plenty of guests do take a dip – especially after a few hours of sun. If you're planning a swim stop, a boat with a swim platform (like the Azimut 39) makes it easy to get in and out.

Air Temperature and Sunshine Hours

Daytime highs in May range from 20°C to 26°C, with overnight lows around 14–16°C. You'll enjoy roughly 9–10 hours of direct sunshine, and the UV index is already strong – so bring SPF 50. Evenings can be a little breezy, so a light jacket is wise for sunset cruises.

Wind and Waves in May

May is generally calm. Typical winds are 10–15 knots, mostly from the west (Poniente) or east (Levante). The Levante can occasionally bring a short chop, but our skippers know the sheltered spots along the coast – like Cala del Faro or Cala Cortés – to keep your ride smooth. Wave heights rarely exceed 0.5–1m in the bay.

Rain Chances in May

May is one of the driest months in Marbella. On average, you can expect only about 4 rainy days across the whole month, and most of those are brief showers. The chance of rain on any given day is around 13%. In short, your charter is very unlikely to be cancelled due to weather.

Best Boats for Spring Conditions

For a group of up to 9–11, the Astondoa 40 (12.5m) and Azimut 39 (12.5m) are ideal – fast, stable, and with plenty of shade. For a larger group (up to 12), the Azimut 58 Flybridge offers a spacious flybridge perfect for soaking up the spring sun. If you want a touch of luxury, the Mangusta 80 (24m) starts at €4,719 for 4 hours and includes a free jet ski.

May Charter Prices and Inclusions

Our Tier A boats – Astondoa 40 and Azimut 39 – are priced at €749 for 2 hours or €2,299 for a full day (8 hours). That includes a licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, and Spanish IVA (21%). No hidden costs. For the Mangusta 80, the minimum charter is 4 hours at €4,719. Other boats are priced on request via WhatsApp – just ask.

Where to Cruise in May

From Puerto Banús, you can head west to the sandbar at Cabopino, or east towards Marbella Marina and the Golden Mile. In May, the sea is calm enough to anchor at Cala del Faro or Cala Cortés – two lovely coves where you can swim and enjoy a picnic. If you have 8 hours, a run down to Estepona or even Sotogrande is very doable.

Booking Tips for May 2025

May weekends and the last two weeks of the month are popular, so book early. We recommend reserving at least 1–2 weeks in advance. You can check availability and get a custom quote via WhatsApp – we usually reply within the hour. And remember, our skippers monitor the weather daily; if conditions are unsafe, we'll reschedule or refund in full.
